references.functional_evidence: [OS2] The mutation p.Arg206His in the ACVR1 gene leads to continuous activation of the BMP signaling pathway, which is responsible for the abnormal bone formation seen in fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva (FOP). Mechanism: gain-of-function Phenotype: abnormal bone formation Biochemistry: dysregulated BMP signaling pathway
references.verbatim_quote: This mutation causes an amino acid change from arginine to histidine at the 206th position of the ACVR1 gene (R206H), leading to the dysregulated BMP signaling pathway observed in FOP.

references.functional_evidence: [OS2] The p.R206H substitution in ACVR1 leads to increased basal canonical signaling activity mediated by phosphorylated SMAD1/5/8, which is thought to provoke the pathological differentiation of local progenitor cells into cartilage and subsequently into bone. Mechanism: gain-of-function Phenotype: ectopic bone formation Biochemistry: increased canonical signaling activity
references.verbatim_quote: The mutations—most commonly an R206H substitution—confer on ALK2 a greater basal canonical signaling activity mediated by phosphorylated suppressor of mother against decapentaplegic (SMAD)1/5/8 but also greater responsiveness of protein ligands including various BMPs and activin A.

references.verbatim_quote: The canonical FOP mutation (c.617G > A, p.R206H) leads to an increased activation of ALK2-mediated signaling, for which different underlying mechanisms have been shown.

references.verbatim_quote: The classic FOP-associated ACVR1 mutation R206H renders ACVR1 constitutively active and increases the phosphorylation of downstream Smad1 effector proteins.

references.verbatim_quote: The R206H variant imparts neofunctional properties to ACVR1, effectively rendering the R206H ACVR1 a neoreceptor.
